cases.sentence: Занимая третий год место начальника одного из ___ в Москве, Степан Аркадьич приобрел, кроме любви, и уважение сослуживцев, подчиненных, начальников и всех, кто имел до него дело.
cases.explain: «присутственных мест» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: After filling for three years the post of president of one of the government boards at Moscow, Stepan Arkadyevitch had won the respect, as well as the liking, of his fellow-officials, subordinates, and superiors, and all who had had business with him. The principal qualities in Stepan Arkadyevitch which had gained him this universal respect in the service consisted, in the first place, of his extreme indulgence for others, founded on a consciousness of his own shortcomings; secondly, of his perfect liberalism—not the liberalism he read of in the papers, but the liberalism that was in his blood, in virtue of which he treated all men perfectly equally and exactly the same, whatever their fortune or calling might be; and thirdly—the most important point—his complete indifference to the business in which he was engaged, in consequence of which he was never carried away, and never made mistakes.

cases.sentence: Приехав к месту своего служения, Степан Аркадьич, провожаемый почтительным швейцаром, с портфелем прошел в свой ___, надел мундир и вошел в присутствие.
cases.explain: «маленький кабинет» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: On reaching the offices of the board, Stepan Arkadyevitch, escorted by a deferential porter with a portfolio, went into his little private room, put on his uniform, and went into the boardroom. The clerks and copyists all rose, greeting him with good-humored deference. Stepan Arkadyevitch moved quickly, as ever, to his place, shook hands with his colleagues, and sat down. He made a joke or two, and talked just as much as was consistent with due decorum, and began work. No one knew better than Stepan Arkadyevitch how to hit on the exact line between freedom, simplicity, and official stiffness necessary for the agreeable conduct of business. A secretary, with the good-humored deference common to everyone in Stepan Arkadyevitch’s office, came up with papers, and began to speak in the familiar and easy tone which had been introduced by Stepan Arkadyevitch.

cases.sentence: Никто вернее Степана Аркадьича не умел найти ту границу свободы, простоты и официальности, которая нужна для ___ делами.
cases.explain: «приятного занятия» — after the preposition «для», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Секретарь весело и почтительно, как и все в присутствии Степана Аркадьича, подошел с бумагами и проговорил тем ___, который введен был Степаном Аркадьичем:
cases.explain: «фамильярно-либеральным тоном» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: On reaching the offices of the board, Stepan Arkadyevitch, escorted by a deferential porter with a portfolio, went into his little private room, put on his uniform, and went into the boardroom. The clerks and copyists all rose, greeting him with good-humored deference. Stepan Arkadyevitch moved quickly, as ever, to his place, shook hands with his colleagues, and sat down. cases.sentence: – Мы таки добились сведения из Пензенского ___.
cases.explain: «губернского правления» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “We have succeeded in getting the information from the government department of Penza. Here, would you care? …”

cases.sentence: «Если б они знали, – думал он, с ___ склонив голову при слушании доклада, – каким виноватым мальчиком полчаса тому назад был их председатель!» – И глаза его смеялись при чтении доклада…
cases.explain: «значительным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “If they knew,” he thought, bending his head with a significant air as he listened to the report, “what a guilty little boy their president was half an hour ago.” And his eyes were laughing during the reading of the report. Till two o’clock the sitting would go on without a break, and at two o’clock there would be an interval and luncheon.

cases.sentence: Еще не было двух часов, когда большие ___ залы присутствия вдруг отворились, и кто-то вошел.
cases.explain: «стеклянные двери» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: It was not yet two, when the large glass doors of the boardroom suddenly opened and someone came in. All the officials sitting on the further side under the portrait of the Tsar and the eagle, delighted at any distraction, looked round at the door; but the doorkeeper standing at the door at once drove out the intruder, and closed the glass door after him.

cases.sentence: Два товарища его, ___ Никитин и камер-юнкер Гриневич, вышли с ним.
cases.explain: «старый служака» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: When the case had been read through, Stepan Arkadyevitch got up and stretched, and by way of tribute to the liberalism of the times took out a cigarette in the boardroom and went into his private room. Two of the members of the board, the old veteran in the service, Nikitin, and the Kammerjunker Grinevitch, went in with him.

cases.sentence: Этот самый, – сказал сторож, указывая на сильно сложенного широкоплечего человека с курчавою бородой, который, не снимая бараньей шапки, быстро и легко взбегал наверх по стертым ступенькам ___.
cases.explain: «каменной лестницы» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Maybe he’s gone into the passage, but here he comes anyway. That is he,” said the doorkeeper, pointing to a strongly built, broad-shouldered man with a curly beard, who, without taking off his sheepskin cap, was running lightly and rapidly up the worn steps of the stone staircase. One of the members going down—a lean official with a portfolio—stood out of his way and looked disapprovingly at the legs of the stranger, then glanced inquiringly at Oblonsky.

cases.sentence: – Имею честь знать вашего брата, Сергея Иваныча, – сказал Гриневич, подавая свою тонкую руку с ___.
cases.explain: «длинными ногтями» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I have the honor of knowing your brother, Sergey Ivanovitch,” said Grinevitch, holding out his slender hand with its long nails.

cases.sentence: – Как же ты говорил, что никогда больше не наденешь ___? – сказал он, оглядывая его новое, очевидно от французского портного, платье. – Так! я вижу: – новая фаза.
cases.explain: «европейского платья» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “How was it you used to say you would never wear European dress again?” he said, scanning his new suit, obviously cut by a French tailor. “Ah! I see: a new phase.”

cases.sentence: – Как же ты говорил, что никогда больше не наденешь европейского платья? – сказал он, оглядывая его новое, очевидно от ___, платье. – Так! я вижу: – новая фаза.
cases.explain: «французского портного» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “How was it you used to say you would never wear European dress again?” he said, scanning his new suit, obviously cut by a French tailor. “Ah! I see: a new phase.”

cases.sentence: – Как же ты говорил, что никогда больше не наденешь европейского платья? – сказал он, оглядывая его новое, очевидно от французского портного, платье. – Так! я вижу: – ___.
cases.explain: «новая фаза» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “How was it you used to say you would never wear European dress again?” he said, scanning his new suit, obviously cut by a French tailor. “Ah! I see: a new phase.”

cases.sentence: И так странно было видеть это умное, мужественное лицо в таком ___, что Облонский перестал смотреть на него.
cases.explain: «детском состоянии» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Levin suddenly blushed, not as grown men blush, slightly, without being themselves aware of it, but as boys blush, feeling that they are ridiculous through their shyness, and consequently ashamed of it and blushing still more, almost to the point of tears. And it was so strange to see this sensible, manly face in such a childish plight, that Oblonsky left off looking at him.

cases.sentence: Он ждал от Левина какой-нибудь ___.
cases.explain: «странной выходки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “What don’t you understand?” said Oblonsky, smiling as brightly as ever, and picking up a cigarette. He expected some queer outburst from Levin.

cases.sentence: – Может быть, и да, – сказал Левин. – Но все-таки я любуюсь на твое величие и горжусь, что у меня друг такой ___.
cases.explain: «великий человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Perhaps so,” said Levin. “But all the same I admire your grandeur, and am proud that I’ve a friend in such a great person. You’ve not answered my question, though,” he went on, with a desperate effort looking Oblonsky straight in the face.

cases.sentence: Однако ты мне не ответил на мой вопрос, – прибавил он, с ___ прямо глядя в глаза Облонскому.
cases.explain: «отчаянным усилием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Perhaps so,” said Levin. “But all the same I admire your grandeur, and am proud that I’ve a friend in such a great person. You’ve not answered my question, though,” he went on, with a desperate effort looking Oblonsky straight in the face.

cases.sentence: Хорошо, как у тебя три тысячи десятин в ___, да такие мускулы, да свежесть, как у двенадцатилетней девочки, – а придешь и ты к нам.
cases.explain: «Каразинском уезде» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Oh, that’s all very well. You wait a bit, and you’ll come to this yourself. It’s very nice for you to have over six thousand acres in the Karazinsky district, and such muscles, and the freshness of a girl of twelve; still you’ll be one of us one day. Yes, as to your question, there is no change, but it’s a pity you’ve been away so long.”

cases.sentence: – Должно быть, очень ___, – сказал Гриневич, когда Левин вышел.
cases.explain: «энергический господин» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That gentleman must be a man of great energy,” said Grinevitch, when Levin had gone away.

cases.sentence: Три тысячи десятин в ___, все впереди, и свежести сколько!
cases.explain: «Каразинском уезде» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Yes, my dear boy,” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, nodding his head, “he’s a lucky fellow! Over six thousand acres in the Karazinsky district; everything before him; and what youth and vigor! Not like some of us.”
